content.user_title: Apply SOLID Principles to TypeScript Code
content.value_statement: Teams often know SOLID terms but struggle to apply them in TypeScript. This skill provides practical refactoring patterns, examples, and review prompts.
actual_capabilities: Explains each SOLID principle for Node.js and TypeScript projects.
Shows before-and-after refactoring examples for service design.
Demonstrates factory functions, abstractions, and dependency injection.
Uses typed Result patterns for validation and error handling examples.
Shows how focused interfaces improve testing and implementation swapping.
Includes practical order-service examples with repositories, payment, and notification boundaries.
limitations: The skill is documentation-only and does not run code or tests.
Examples focus on TypeScript and Node.js rather than every language.
The sample code is illustrative and may need project-specific adaptation.
It does not replace architecture review for complex production systems.

use_cases.title: Refactor Service Classes
use_cases.description: Break large TypeScript services into validation, persistence, payment, and notification responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Changes
use_cases.description: Check new modules for SOLID violations before merging feature work.

use_cases.title: Teach Practical Design
use_cases.description: Use concrete TypeScript examples to explain SOLID tradeoffs during mentoring or onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Single Responsibility Principle for a TypeScript service. Use one small before-and-after example and list one testability benefit.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript module for SOLID violations. Focus on responsibility boundaries, abstractions, and dependencies. Suggest a minimal refactor plan.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Toward SOLID
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this order workflow toward SOLID design. Separate validation, persistence, payment, and notification concerns. Keep behavior unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Design Extensible Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a TypeScript architecture for this feature using SOLID principles. Define interfaces, dependency injection points, tests, and extension paths.

output_examples.input: A service validates orders, charges payments, saves records, and emails users.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify a Single Responsibility violation and propose separate validation, payment, repository, and notification modules.

output_examples.input: A discount function has many conditionals for membership types.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend strategy functions or a registry so new discounts can be added without changing existing logic.

output_examples.input: A module directly creates its database client inside business logic.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest an abstraction for the repository and inject the implementation from the composition layer.

best_practices: Start with the smallest responsibility split that improves readability or testing.
Use interfaces or function types where a dependency may change or needs a test double.
Keep refactors behavior-preserving before adding new features or abstractions.
anti_patterns: Do not create abstractions only to satisfy a principle label.
Do not hide business rules behind generic names or unclear factories.
Do not combine validation, persistence, integration calls, and notification in one workflow function.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or modify files?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for reviewing or refactoring TypeScript code.

faq.question: Which languages does it target?
faq.answer: It targets TypeScript and Node.js, with functional patterns that may translate to similar languages.

faq.question: Can it help with tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show dependency injection and focused interfaces that make tests easier to write.

faq.question: Is every SOLID principle always useful?
faq.answer: No. The skill encourages practical refactoring only when it improves change safety, clarity, or testability.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include real project examples?
faq.answer: It includes an e-commerce order workflow example with validation, pricing, repositories, payment, notification, and tests.
